correctness.rationale: Let d=4c. No discriminant x²-d vanishes; counting (x-z)(x+z)=d gives the sum of its characters as -1, so exactly (q+1)/2 coefficients are allowed with zero included. χ(-d)=-χ(-1) shows that deleting zero leaves more than half of the group for q≡3 and exactly half for q≡1 mod 4. In the latter case x→(±d)/x flips the discriminant character, excluding ±d. If another t were excluded, the two disjoint half-size sets would partition the group and the quartic F(x)=(x²-d)(t²-dx²) would have nonsquare value everywhere, including zero. Its four roots are distinct for t²≠d²; its squarefree double cover has genus one and its nonsquare leading coefficient excludes rational points at infinity. Hasse–Weil excludes the resulting zero point count over any odd prime power. The sharpened check 4N(t)=#C_t(F_q) for nonsingular t follows by expanding the product of the two nonsquare indicators, summing over x≠0 and accounting for x=0 and infinity. The size sum (q-3)+(q-1)/2 exceeds q-1 precisely when q>5; for q=5 the two allowed coefficients are opposite and all triple products give exactly two values.
residual_risks: Independent checks were finite and prime-field only; the character count and genus-one argument apply to all odd prime powers.
